notes: Reference corpus; deliverables in research/corpora/rpatters1-main/. Published findings cite it. 1150 distinct source hashes across 1289 loose files; 2042 exports present, 1189 matched adjacent-exact, 36 fallback-unique, 29 fallback-ambiguous, 35 unmatched. Archive members included: 2438 occurrences, 1520 distinct, from 509 archives (2468 candidate members rejected as not Finale content). corpus_fingerprint covers loose files only, so it is comparable across runs with and without archives. Re-surveyed on the date shown after the banner pattern was widened to the Finale 1.0.0 spelling and AppleDouble sidecars were excluded from discovery; the count fell from 1290 to 1289 and the fingerprint changed accordingly, because one 4096-byte ._ sidecar that had been carried as an unknown-product row is now correctly not a specimen. No file changed saving product. Surveyed without --sniff-content: every source here is named *.mus.

Finale application installations for macOS and Windows, Finale 1.0.0 through Finale 2010, rather than authored documents; deliverables in research/corpora/rpatters1-installs/. 4307 distinct source hashes across 9740 loose files, so this corpus is heavily duplicated across versions. No exports and no MUSX counterparts exist, so export_suffix is set to match nothing and the semantic half of the pipeline was skipped: there are no record_correlations.csv or RECORD_CATALOG.md deliverables. Surveyed with --sniff-content, which supplied 2198 of the specimens; the remaining 7542 are named *.mus. Classic Mac Finale kept the file type in the resource fork, so an extension-only scan would have found zero files for products 1.0.0, 2.6, 3.0, 3.2, 3.5, 3.7, 3.8, 97, 98 and 99. Archives were scanned (32 legacy installer ZIPs) and yielded no cacheable members: 373 candidate members were all rejected as not Finale content. Excluded from the scan: 'Finale PDK' (MakeMusic proprietary PDK sources, deliberately outside this project's provenance boundary); '*.lib' and '*.fan' (Finale library and font-annotation files, ENIGMA-framed but not documents); '*.fpa' (SmartMusic files, a different application's format that carries a Finale banner); and the Finale 2014.5/25/26/27 application bundles (MUSX-era only). Exclusion matching is case-insensitive, which matters here: this corpus carries .MUS, .FPA, .LIB, .Lib and .FAN from DOS and Windows filesystems. ETF files are rejected by content rather than by name, because an ETF quotes the product banner on its fourth line and two of them here are extensionless. The library directories themselves are NOT excluded: they contain no .mus file but do contain real documents, because at version 2007 Finale moved two stock font-default documents into them. corpus_fingerprint covers loose files only.
